title: Square a racked two-rail gantry beam by moving both carriages onto their front end stops together
instruction: Move the gantry beam's two carriages forward along the rails until both rest against their front stops, then let go with both grippers.
context: Squaring a gantry is a routine step when building or servicing a 3D printer, CNC router or Cartesian robot: with the belts loose, the beam is run onto both end stops together so it sits square. Pushed at one end only, the beam racks, its two carriages bind on the rails by friction, and it stops short. Robot-building and robot-servicing work like this is what an autonomous robot workforce for hardware assembly must learn.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475. (1) Two linear rails, MGN12 pattern, hardened steel, 12 mm wide x 8 mm high x 250 mm long, grey (0.62,0.64,0.68), fixed to the table along x from x 0.030 to 0.280 at y +0.170 and -0.170 (340 mm apart), friction 0.2. Each rail has a ball groove down both sides: foot 12 x 3 mm, neck 8 x 2 mm (groove 2 mm high, 2 mm deep), head 12 x 3 mm. (2) Two end-stop blocks, steel, red (0.80,0.10,0.10), 10 x 30 x 13 mm, fixed at the front end of each rail, stop face at x 0.280. (3) Two captured carriage blocks, MGN12H size, grey steel, 45.4 x 27 x 13 mm each, friction 0.2: a top plate on the rail head, two side walls 7.25 mm thick that wrap the rail with 0.25 mm clearance a side, their bottoms 3 mm above the table, and on each wall a 1.5 mm high lip that sits in the rail groove, 0.25 mm above the foot, 0.25 mm under the head and 0.25 mm off the neck. The lips lie under the rail head, so the beam cannot be lifted more than 0.25 mm off its rails; it can only be slid. A real MGN12H carriage is held on its rail the same way by its recirculating balls in the same groove. (4) Beam, 20 x 20 x 400 mm aluminium extrusion, silver (0.78,0.80,0.84), bolted across the two blocks at y -200 to +200, with an orange toolhead 40 x 50 x 40 mm on its front at its centre; beam, blocks and toolhead 0.80 kg together. The beam starts racked, yawed -0.45 deg about the vertical: its centre at x 0.2160, the left block 2.7 mm ahead of the right, the left front face 40 mm and the right 42.7 mm short of the stops. Belts omitted (loose). Both arms start at the ready pose.
scoring: Only the end state counts, and only travel made by sliding on the rails; a harmless moment (a fast push, a brief lift with no travel) zeroes nothing. A carriage is on its rail when its block sits at seated height (every top corner within 1 mm), within 0.6 mm of the rail centreline, yawed under 0.7 deg, and between the rail's rear end and the stop face (no front corner more than 0.5 mm past it). Slide credit = each front face's forward travel summed over steps where that carriage was on its rail. Ladder: 0.25 both carriages were slid at least 25 mm forward; 0.5 both on their rails at the end, the whole way slid (within 2 mm of the total displacement), every front corner within 5 mm of its stop; 0.75 as 0.5 but face to face and seated: every front corner of both blocks within 0.05 mm of its stop face (not more than 0.10 mm past it) and every top corner within 0.5 mm of seated height; 1.0 also the beam under 3 mm/s for 1 s (60 fps video) and both grippers at least 30 mm clear of the beam and under 5 mm/s for 1 s (release gate). A beam lifted off its rails and set down on the stops scores 0. Real trial: 0.05 mm feeler gauge at both corners of each stop face, a dial gauge or feeler at the block ends for height, tape for 25 mm and 5 mm, video for stillness and for the slide.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Slide both carriages back along the rails until the left front face is 40 mm and the right 42.7 mm from its stop (tape), the beam racked with the left end ahead; the beam sits on the two blocks with the toolhead at its centre. The carriages stay on their rails (retained by the groove lips; refit them from the rail's rear end if removed). Wipe the rails dry; check a 0.2 mm feeler passes the clearance at each block's side.
fidelity: Rigid-body model: each carriage is an MGN12H-size block whose two 1.5 mm lips sit in a 2 mm ball groove of the rail (a simplification of the ball grooves), 0.25 mm clearance on every face, so it cannot be lifted off. Recirculating balls and preload are not modelled. Racking and binding come from contact friction (0.2); nothing is scripted. Beam, blocks and toolhead are one 0.8 kg body; belts, motors and endstop switches are left out.
scores: Not re-run on this revision (no simulator time left); previous revision: demo 1.0
